new_statements.quote: Practically all autochthonous Soqotri words and forms are stressed on the penultimate syllable. The only systematic exception is the short prefix conjugation of the basic stem, stressed on the last syllable of the base: lˠaʕdɛ́g ‘may I suckle (intrans.)’. Since such forms can be opposed to the short prefix conjugation of the causative stem (lˠáʕdɛg ‘may I/she suckle (trans.)’), one has to acknowledge that the position of the accent has some phonemic load. [...] The initial cluster can be broken with an epenthetic e (or a if the preceding consonant is ħ). The resulting forms may give the impression of being abnormally stressed on the second syllable. However, this incongruency can be avoided if one treats the first vowel as a phonetic epenthesis
new_statements.citation: Kogan, Leonid & Maria Bulakh. 2019. Soqotri. In John Huehnergard & Na'ama Pat-El (eds.), The Semitic Languages, 2nd edition, 280-320. London/New York: Routledge.
new_statements.locator: sec. 3.3 'Accent and syllable structure', pp. 287-288 (PDF p. 8-9); cf. also p. 282 (parasitic h bullet)
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened (41 pp., InDesign typeset, text layer; printed pp. 280-320). extracted text of PDF p. 8 (printed p. 287) gives sec. 3.3 'Accent and syllable structure' exactly as quoted: 'Practically all autochthonous Soqotri words and forms are stressed on the penultimate syllable. The only systematic exception is the short prefix conjugation of the basic stem, stressed on the last syllable of the base: lˠaʕdɛ́g ‘may I suckle (intrans.)’. Since such forms can be opposed to the short prefix conjugation of the causative stem (lˠáʕdɛg ‘may I/she suckle (trans.)’), one has to acknowledge that the position of the accent has some phonemic load.' The [...] in the quote elides the two sentences on tri-/qua…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress is fixed on the penultimate syllable in native vocabulary; the one systematic exception is the jussive (short prefix conjugation) of the basic stem, which is stressed on the final syllable of the base and thereby contrasts minimally with the causative jussive (penultimate), giving accent a marginal phonemic load; apparent exceptions with stress after a cluster-breaking vowel are analysed as epenthesis, and (per Naumkin et al. 2016: 36) when a prefix vowel is syncopated stress moves to the last syllable rather than onto an epenthetic vowel.
new_statements.exceptions: Short prefix conjugation (jussive) of the basic stem stressed on the last syllable of the base (lˠaʕdɛ́g vs causative lˠáʕdɛg); recent Arabisms implicitly outside the rule ('autochthonous'); epenthetic e/a after initial clusters not counted as a syllable for stress; Naumkin et al. 2016 add: if the imperfect prefix vowel is syncopated, stress falls on the last syllable. Historical note p. 282: 'general shift of the stress to the penultimate syllable' created the parasitic h. Other authors frame it more loosely: Simeone-Senelle 1997/2003 'penultimate or antepenultimate', 'towards the beginning of the word'; Dufour 2022 'generally/predominantly penultimate', phonetic nature of Soqotri stress still undescribed.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level ('words and forms'), citation/elicited forms and corpus texts of the central-eastern (Da'rho) variety; K&B transcribe stress with an acute on every polysyllabic example. Dufour 2022 cautions that what is transcribed as stress in Soqotri is a recent prosodic development whose phonetic exponent is not yet analysed.
new_statements.identity_note: Kogan & Bulakh 2019 explicitly describe the variety of the Da'rho tribe, central-eastern inland Soqotra (the 'rather uniform central-eastern variety' spoken by about two thirds of the island); glottocode soqo1240 (no Glottolog sub-dialect codes). The western Qalansiya dialect (Makhashen 2009) and 'Abd-el-Kuri (Wagner 1959) are not covered by the quoted statement. Simeone-Senelle's 1997/2003 remarks draw on several dialects (Qadhub, Hadibo, Haghier, Diksam, Qalansiya).

sources.note: Sec. 3.3 'Accent and syllable structure' (p. 287): practically all autochthonous words and forms are stressed on the penultimate syllable; only systematic exception is the short prefix conjugation (jussive) of the basic stem, stressed on the last syllable of the base (lˠaʕdɛ́g vs causative lˠáʕdɛg), so accent position has 'some phonemic load'; apparent second-syllable stress after cluster-breaking epenthetic e/a is treated as epenthesis. p. 282: parasitic h arose when long vowels lost their accent 'due to the general shift of the stress to the penultimate syllable'. Variety described: Da'rho…

sources.citation: Dufour, Julien. 2022. Vowel Quality as a History Maker: Stress, Metaphony and the Renewal of Proto-Semitic Morphology in Modern South Arabian. In P. Epps, D. Law & N. Pat-El (eds.), Historical Linguistics and Endangered Languages, 56-96. Routledge. HAL halshs-03988300.
sources.note: Sec. 3.3.2 (pp. 69-70): 'What linguists, with some amount of hesitation, transcribe as stress in modern Soqotri has apparently no connection in its position with the stress of continental MSA languages and is generally penultimate'; fn. 17 'The modern stress (predominantly penultimate)'; argues modern Soqotri stress is a new prosodic feature unrelated to Proto-MSA stress (whose reflex is the Soqotri 'stable vowel'); p. 89 calls a fine-grained analysis of modern Soqotri stress a desideratum.

sources.citation: Naumkin, V., M. Bulakh, D. Cherkashin, L. Kogan, A. Issa & I. Gumaan. 2016. Studies in the Verbal Morphology of Soqotri II: Weak and Geminated Roots in the Basic Stem. Zeitschrift für Arabische Linguistik 63: 19ff. (HSE repository offprint, guest-readable)
sources.note: Sec. 2.1.2, p. 36: 'Since the base of the imperfect is monosyllabic, the general rule of penultimate stress leads to the prefix vowel being accented in most of the forms. However, if the vowel of the prefix is syncopated, the stress shifts to the last syllable (rather than the epenthetic vowel after the second radical)'. Confirms penultimate default.

sources.note: Sec. 1.1.6: parasitic h is related to 'the rules of stress in S: stress falls on the penultimate or antepenultimate syllable'; sec. 1.3.1 'Syllabic structure and stress': in Mehri/Hobyot/Bathari/Harsusi stress is on the last long syllable or first syllable; 'In S, the general trend is to have the stress towards the beginning of the word', which led to vowel splitting via parasitic h.
